lead.headline: Nvidia Clears the Bar and Steadies a Shaken Market
lead.dek: A $115.8 billion quarter and a $130 billion forecast lift futures after a two-day rout that sent the S&P 500 to its lowest close since July.
body: Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion after Tuesday's close, up 103% on the year and roughly $6 billion above the consensus of about $109 billion. Adjusted earnings came in at $2.68 a share against forecasts near $2.47. Data-centre revenue alone reached $107.6 billion.

The forward numbers did the heavier lifting. Interim chief executive Colette Kress guided the fourth quarter to about $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, ahead of the roughly $125 billion analysts expected, and raised the company's fiscal 2028 growth outlook to about 75% from 70%. She also put the cloud industry's revenue backlog at $2.5 trillion.

It was Nvidia's first report since Jensen Huang resigned on 12 November. On the call, board chair Harvey Jones said the board has no intention of reinstating him, closing a door that a petition, several Silicon Valley figures and President Trump had tried to hold open.

The relief arrived after a bruising stretch. On Tuesday the Dow fell 849 points, more than 1,000 at the low, as a report of an outage on a classified NSA network rattled traders already selling software and chip stocks. The S&P 500 finished at 7,340.53, its lowest close since late July, and every one of its 11 sectors fell. Nvidia rose about 3% before Wednesday's open and Nasdaq-100 futures gained roughly 0.8%.

impact.title: What it means for markets
points: Chips and AI infrastructure lead the rebound: Nvidia, CoreWeave, Nebius, AMD, Dell and Sandisk were higher before the open, and Korean and Taiwanese chip names bounced overnight.
The beat answers the demand question but not the governance one. A leaderless Nvidia, wider US export curbs and a 5%+ 10-year yield still cap how far valuations can stretch.
Watch the Nasdaq-100 near 27,600: it needs to finish November above roughly that level to avoid its worst November since 2008.

highlights.text: Nvidia beats and raises; US futures rebound led by chips after the S&P 500's lowest close since July.
Washington widens AI-chip curbs to data centres in Thailand and Malaysia; ASML and BE Semiconductor fall, DAX drops 2.1% on Tuesday.
A December Fed hike is about 95% priced; the 10-year sits near 5.11% and the October minutes land at 20:00 CET tonight.
Gold slips under $3,800 and bitcoin hovers near $64,000 as rate-hike bets firm the dollar.
Xi greets Trump on the tarmac in Shenzhen; a first US-China-Russia leaders' meeting is set for Thursday at APEC.
Iran fires drones at a US radar in Bahrain; the US strikes an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island. Brent still falls toward $92.
Sensex sheds 500 points as India's 13% rally pauses, even as foreign inflows top a record $10 billion this month.
Berlin's coalition agrees to cut the electricity tax for 2027, a relief package costing about €5.4 billion a year.
Anthropic prices its IPO tonight ahead of a Nasdaq debut as ANT on Thursday, at up to about $1.4 trillion.
Deutsche Bank falls more than 6% after a 15-million-file leak revisits old client dealings.

read.title: The Ledger's Read
paragraphs: Three currents run through today's paper. The first is the AI trade being repriced. Nvidia's numbers say demand is intact, but investors are now pricing risks that sit outside the income statement: who runs the company, what Washington lets it sell, and where Chinese buyers can rent computing power. Expect a chip-led bounce; whether it lasts depends more on those three questions than on the next quarter.

The second is the cost of money. With a December Fed hike close to fully priced, the 10-year Treasury above 5% and the October minutes due tonight, rates are the tide under every boat. Higher-for-longer weighs most on long-duration assets: unprofitable tech, gold and bitcoin all fell this week while the dollar firmed and the euro touched a one-year low.

The third is rotation. Money that is leaving crowded US tech is finding India, where foreign investors have put a record $10 billion to work in November, and defensive corners of Europe. Cheaper oil, with Brent down around 16% over the past month despite fresh Gulf skirmishes, helps both: it cools inflation for importers such as India and Germany. Today's question for portfolios is whether the Nvidia relief marks a floor for tech or just a pause in the rotation.

sections.name: Markets & Money
sections.intro: The finance pages: every story here ends with what it means for prices.

stories.headline: Two-Day Slide Drags the S&P 500 to a Five-Month Low
stories.summary: Selling spread well beyond tech on Tuesday. The Dow lost 848.75 points, or 1.64%, after falling more than 1,000 at its low, and all 11 S&P 500 sectors finished lower. Software led the decline, with Salesforce, Intuit and ServiceNow among the worst performers, while Home Depot fell about 6% after cutting its outlook. A CNN report that a classified NSA network had gone down added to the nerves; the agency later described it as a temporary degradation during routine maintenance. The VIX closed near 26.
stories.market: A broad de-risking rather than a tech-only story: financials were the weakest sector, and decliners beat gainers more than five to one. The Nasdaq-100 was down about 4.2% for November as of Monday.

stories.headline: Target and Lowe's Beat, but the Quality of the Beat Is Questioned
stories.summary: Target raised its full-year net sales growth forecast to about 6% from about 5%. Lowe's earned an adjusted $3.10 a share against roughly $2.89 expected, but 34 cents came from tariff refunds; its gross margin slipped to about 33% and it trimmed its operating-margin outlook to around 11.5%. Both stocks slipped before the open.
stories.market: The US consumer is still spending, but one-off tariff refunds are flattering some retail earnings. Investors are paying for margins, not headline beats.

stories.headline: Anthropic Prices the Year's Biggest AI Listing Tonight
stories.summary: Anthropic is due to set its IPO price on Wednesday evening, US time, with Nasdaq trading under the ticker ANT expected on Thursday. It is offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78, which would raise up to about $64 billion and value the company at roughly $1.4 trillion at the top of the range. Some reports suggest strong demand could push the price above the range.
stories.market: A direct read on appetite for AI after a punishing month for the sector. A deal this size also draws cash that could otherwise sit in the existing AI megacaps.

stories.headline: US Chip Curbs Knock Europe; the DAX Fights for 26,000
stories.summary: Washington broadened its controls on advanced AI chips, restricting shipments to data centres in Thailand and Malaysia that some Chinese firms used to rent computing power. European chip names including ASML, BE Semiconductor and AT&S fell. The DAX lost 2.08% on Tuesday to 26,045, the Euro Stoxx 50 dropped 2.15% and London's FTSE 100 had its worst day in eight months. Nvidia's results gave Frankfurt a small lift at Wednesday's open, but the index was flat near 26,050 by midday, after topping 27,000 for the first time last week.
stories.market: European chip-equipment makers carry the most direct exposure to tighter China rules. Beijing called the move economic coercion and promised a response, a risk for exporters ahead of Thursday's leaders' meeting.

stories.headline: Deutsche Bank Slides on a 15-Million-File Leak
stories.summary: Deutsche Bank shares fell more than 6% on Tuesday, their biggest drop since April 2025, after a consortium of outlets including Der Spiegel, the Financial Times and the New York Times published reports from leaked internal records. The reports cover past dealings with Russian oligarchs, Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein. The bank said the matters date back many years and that its controls have since been strengthened.
stories.market: Headline and regulatory risk rather than a balance-sheet problem for now; analysts flagged the chance of further revelations from the trove.

stories.headline: Sensex Sheds 500 Points as the November Rally Takes a Breather
stories.summary: Indian benchmarks fell on Wednesday from near nine-month highs. The Sensex lost 500.38 points to 82,031.81 and the Nifty 50 fell 159.45 points to 25,227.95, both down about 0.6%. Metals, autos, IT, consumer durables and financials led the decline, and the Nifty Midcap 100 lost 1.2%. The pullback followed a 13% rally in 12 sessions; on Tuesday the Nifty Bank index had closed at a record 62,273.
stories.market: Profit-taking after a sharp run, with domestic institutions selling into foreign buying. The trend is still supported by record inflows and cheaper oil.

stories.headline: Chips Lift Seoul While Hong Kong Lags on New Curbs
stories.summary: Korea's Kospi rose 1.99% to 5,067 as chip heavyweights recovered on Nvidia's numbers, and Japan's Nikkei 225 added 0.28% to 59,024 after Japan reported October exports up 20.5% on the year. Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 0.91% to 23,295, weighed by the new US export rules, while mainland China's CSI 300 edged up 0.18%.
stories.market: Asia splits along the chip-curb line: suppliers to Nvidia gain, Chinese tech and Hong Kong lose. The yen near 159.5 per dollar keeps Japanese exporters supported.

stories.headline: A December Fed Hike Is Now All but Certain
stories.summary: Futures price about a 95% chance that the Federal Reserve, led by Chair Kevin Warsh, raises rates by a quarter point on 9 December from the current 3.75% to 4.00% range. Treasury yields eased slightly on Tuesday, with the 10-year at 5.109%, the 2-year at 4.806% and the 30-year near 5.46%. October retail sales rose 0.2%, in line, but sales excluding autos and gas jumped 0.6% against 0.4% expected. Governor Christopher Waller has said he could back a half-point move if core inflation keeps printing 0.3% or more. Minutes of the October meeting are due at 20:00 CET tonight.
stories.market: A 10-year yield above 5% is the single biggest weight on equity valuations right now. Hawkish minutes would push the dollar up and gold, bitcoin and long-duration tech down; key data before the meeting are October core PCE on 25 November and November payrolls on 4 December.

stories.headline: ECB Weighs a December Hike as the Euro Hits a One-Year Low
stories.summary: The ECB held rates at its October meeting but warned that energy costs are lifting inflation risks, and President Christine Lagarde, who steps down early on 7 February, said the bank is watching data to judge whether a December hike is needed. The ECB's euro reference rate fell to 1.0989 dollars on Tuesday, below last week's 52-week low.
stories.market: A weaker euro helps German and French exporters but imports inflation, which strengthens the case for the ECB to follow the Fed.

stories.headline: Gold Breaks Below $3,800
stories.summary: Gold fell about 2% on Wednesday to roughly $3,771 an ounce, down nearly 9% over the past month and far below January's record of about $5,608. Futures opened at their lowest level since late September before falling further.
stories.market: Rising real yields and a firmer dollar are draining the haven trade. A hawkish read of tonight's Fed minutes is the next risk.

stories.headline: Oil Slips Even as the Gulf Flares
stories.summary: Brent fell 1.6% to about $91.70 a barrel and WTI to about $84 on Wednesday, despite overnight Iranian drone launches at Bahrain and a US strike on Qeshm Island. A build in US inventories and an IEA view that the market returns to surplus this quarter outweighed the headlines. Brent is down about 16% over the past month on hopes of a US-Iran settlement.
stories.market: Cheaper crude is a gift to oil importers such as India and Germany and to airlines, and a drag on energy stocks. The market is treating the Bahrain incidents as noise unless Hormuz flows are hit.

stories.headline: Bitcoin Gives Back Its Nvidia Bounce
stories.summary: Bitcoin traded near $64,100 on Wednesday morning, down about 21% from a month ago and roughly 31% below its level a year earlier. A brief lift after Nvidia's results faded within the hour.
stories.market: Crypto is trading as a high-beta rates asset: the same hike bets weighing on gold are weighing here.

stories.headline: Xi Meets Trump on the Tarmac as APEC Opens in Shenzhen
stories.summary: President Trump arrived in Shenzhen for the APEC summit, his second China visit this year, and was greeted at the airport by Xi Jinping, a gesture Chinese media described as unprecedented for Xi as president. At the welcome banquet Trump shook hands with Vladimir Putin. The three leaders are due to hold a first-ever trilateral meeting on Thursday, with Iran on the agenda. Xi opened the summit with calls for free trade and cooperation on AI.
stories.market: The warm optics collide with this week's US chip curbs, which Beijing condemned. Any trade or export-control thaw would help Hong Kong tech and chip-equipment makers; a breakdown would hit them.

stories.headline: Ukraine Peace Push Moves to Berlin
stories.summary: Ukraine held online talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and European officials, and the parties agreed to meet the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin. Kushner said progress was being made, but the Kremlin said it had not agreed to Europeans joining the next round. EU governments accused Moscow of stalling while striking power plants ahead of winter.
stories.market: A credible deal would weigh on European defence names such as Rheinmetall and on gas prices; continued strikes on energy infrastructure keep a floor under both.

stories.headline: Iran Targets US Radar in Bahrain; US Strikes Back at Qeshm
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards launched drones at a US radar installation at Bahrain's Isa Air Base on Tuesday, their third claimed attack on US radar in Bahrain in under a week. US Central Command said the drones were intercepted without damage. US jets then struck an IRGC missile-launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, and a tanker crew was reported missing in the strait, even as Oman and Qatar continue mediating.
stories.market: Shipping insurance and tanker rates stay elevated, but crude is not pricing escalation. A strike that disrupts Hormuz flows would reverse the month's oil slide quickly.

stories.headline: Merz Coalition Agrees to Cut the Electricity Tax for 2027
stories.summary: After more than eight hours of overnight talks, Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservatives and the Social Democrats agreed to cut the electricity tax for households and more businesses to the EU minimum of 0.1 cents per kilowatt hour, a reduction of about 2 cents. The measure costs around €5.4 billion a year, is funded from surplus renewable-energy money, and for now applies only to 2027; funding from 2028 has not been agreed. The deal defuses a dispute that had become a test of Merz's credibility after state-election defeats in September.
stories.market: Modest relief for energy-intensive industry and household spending power. The stop-gap funding adds to questions about Germany's fiscal path, already flagged by the government's economic advisers.

stories.headline: Economic Advisers Raise Germany's Growth Forecast, Warn on Deficits
stories.summary: Germany's Council of Economic Experts significantly raised its growth forecasts last week, while urging the government to rein in spending on defence and pensions to get widening deficits under control. Merz called the upgrade encouraging for businesses and households.
stories.market: Better growth supports domestic cyclicals and the DAX's mid-caps; heavier borrowing means more Bund supply and upward pressure on yields.

stories.headline: Record Foreign Money Pours Into Indian Stocks
stories.summary: Foreign institutional investors have bought more than $10 billion of Indian equities in November, the largest monthly inflow on record, as funds diversify away from the crowded US AI trade and reward resilient September-quarter balance sheets. Falling crude, from about $118 to the low $90s, has helped. The rupee touched a seven-month high on Wednesday before closing flat at 93.44 per dollar, well off May's low of 96.96.
stories.market: Supports banks, large caps and the rupee. Analysts warn that a rebound in oil, sticky inflation or a turn in the global AI trade could reverse flows quickly.

stories.headline: Inflation Breaches the RBI Band; Goldman Sees Three More Hikes
stories.summary: Consumer inflation rose to 6.1% in October from 5.5% in September, above the top of the RBI's 2% to 6% tolerance band. Goldman Sachs expects three more rate hikes from the central bank, believes the worst is over for the rupee, and has set a Nifty target of 28,500.
stories.market: Higher rates favour bank margins but weigh on rate-sensitive sectors such as autos, real estate and consumer durables, which led Wednesday's decline.

stories.headline: China's Economy Loses Steam in October
stories.summary: Industrial output grew 4.8% on the year in October, below the 5.3% expected and slower than September's 5.5%. Retail sales rose just 0.4%, against forecasts of 0.8%, and fixed-asset investment shrank 8.1% in the first ten months. Economists at ING called it a worrying start to the quarter and urged more policy support.
stories.market: Weak domestic demand keeps pressure on Hong Kong-listed consumer names and industrial metals, while raising the odds of fresh stimulus from Beijing.

stories.headline: Japan's Exports Jump 20.5% as the Yen Stays Weak
stories.summary: Japanese exports rose 20.5% on the year in October, though the trade balance remained in deficit at about ¥476.5 billion. The yen traded near 159.5 per dollar.
stories.market: A weak yen keeps exporters such as automakers and machinery firms competitive and supports the Nikkei near 59,000.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Board Shuts the Door on a Huang Comeback
stories.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive on 12 November amid reports of extramarital relationships, including one with a woman believed to be a Chinese intelligence asset. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO and Harvey Jones the company's first board chair. Huang said this week he would be honoured to return, a petition backing him gathered more than 190,000 signatures, and President Trump said he would not mind a reinstatement. On Tuesday's call, Jones said the board has no such intention.
stories.market: Removes one source of uncertainty but leaves the world's most important AI supplier without a permanent leader during a CEO search. Expect key-person risk to keep a discount on the shares.

stories.headline: Home Depot Cuts Its Outlook
stories.summary: Home Depot shares fell about 6% on Tuesday after the home-improvement chain lowered its outlook, a day before rival Lowe's reported a beat flattered by tariff refunds.
stories.market: Housing-linked retail remains the weak spot of US consumer spending while mortgage rates track a 10-year yield above 5%.
